slides.title: PHRASES MEANING EXAMPLE THIRD TIME’S A CHARM The third time you do something it will finally work. I had to ask her out three times before she said yes. Well you know… Third time’s a charm. IT’S HIGH TIME It’s the right time to do something, or past the appropriate time to do something. It’s high time he met with me to resolve this issue. TIME FLIES Time passes extremely quickly. Kids are growing up so fast; time flies. BEAT THE CLOCK Finish something before time is up, before a deadline. Although she was late to the exam, she managed to beat the clock and finished all of it 10 minutes before the end. AT THE ELEVENTH HOUR Almost too late or at the last possible moment. We barely made the deadline, there was so much to do in this project we turned it in at the eleventh hour. IN THE LONG RUN In the long term, over a long period of time. I hate having so much after school activities now, but I know in the long run this will be beneficial for me. IN THE NICK OF TIME At the last possible moment, just before it’s too late. I made it to the wedding in the nick of time, I almost missed the ceremony. SHIP HAS SAILED A lost opportunity, missed shot. -I should call Annie, -Sorry Chad, that ship has sailed. She got married last month.

slides.title: We are able to express ideas about things or events yet to happen through two main grammar structures.
visibleTexts: We are able to express ideas about things or events yet to happen through two main grammar structures.

FUTURE PERFECT FUTURE CONTINUOUS The guests are coming at 8PM. I’ll have finished cooking by then. In two years’ time, I’ll have had my kids, so I’ll be a parent. Will the kids have gone to bed when I get back? When you get out of the office tomorrow, I’ll be boarding a plane. Come on July, I won’t be working then. Will you be starting work earlier with your new job? To Consider 1. Future perfect works with Will + Have + Past participle. 2. It uses time phrases like: By then, In some years’ time, when clauses, by the time, etc. 3. Future continuous works with To be + V(ing). 4. The time phrases for future continuous may be shared with future perfect; though, the ones used here are more specific as seen in the examples. 5. Both can add Wh words to make questions.

slides.title: We can use the grammar presented to talk about the following function:
visibleTexts: We can use the grammar presented to talk about the following function:

Functions Examples 1 Talk about events that will be completed before a specific time in the future Joseph will have been gone by the time she realizes his feelings. 2 Express actions that will be in progress at a specific time in the future. The police will be setting a perimeter, once the concert starts.

To consider Future continuous may also be used to talk about actions we see as new, different or temporary. E.G: Today we're taking the bus but next week we'll be taking the train. He'll be staying with his parents for several months while his father is in recovery. Will he be starting work later with your new job?

C. Read the following paragraph and have a discussion with the teacher. After that, read the text aloud to your teacher. Check the full article in the link below.

The expert guide to space colonies With our rising planet’s population competing for space and resources, some people are convinced we need to look beyond Earth to help ensure humanity’s survival; What will we have had when that time comes?. As Elon Musk, the entrepreneur behind space tourism company SpaceX put it recently: “I think there is a strong argument for making life multiplanetary in order to safeguard the existence of humanity in the event that something catastrophic were to happen.” Even if you don’t believe this bleak vision, it’s hard to ignore the eternal human instinct to discover the undiscovered – an urge that could push people beyond the safety of our planet, and we reckon we will be doing something about it when time comes. And there might not be as many hurdles as you might think. “We are at the level of technology where we can imagine leaving the planet for a few nearby places in our Solar System,” former astronaut Jeffrey Hoffman, who will present his ideas at our summit, told BBC Future previously. “The Moon is just around the corner, and Mars isn’t that far away. We have the possibility of at least making the first steps of those voyages in our own lifetimes.” What could a space colony look like? One possible idea goes as far back as the 1920s. Austro-Hungarian rocket pioneer Herman Potočnik imagined a circular spacecraft - rather like a flying saucer – that rotates to create artificial gravity while a large, concave mirror could focus sunlight for an energy source. As far-fetched as this may sound, the idea has lingered over the years – most notably in the mid-1970s by the late Princeton physicist Gerard O’Neill, and again by the space think tank British Interplanetary Society. Before you dismiss the idea of floating colonies completely, it’s worth noting that the British Interplanetary Society predicted we would reach the Moon three decades before it actually happened, so imagine where it will have gotten once it sets its mind on it. Adapted from: https://www.bbc.com/future/article/20141002-time-to-plan-a-space-colony
